records.title: A Life Worth Living: Meaning, Morals and Money
records.header: RELIG 101 A Life Worth Living: Meaning, Morals and Money (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 101 A Life Worth Living: Meaning, Morals and Money (5) SSc Investigates how to create meaning in religious and humanistic traditions, how to develop ethical traditions that enable trust and a thriving social order, and the relationship between money and meaning. Students ask what makes life worth living and discover sources of meaning and ethical maxims, as well as tools to navigate decision-making and fashion a flourishing life.

records.title: Jesus: A Global Biography
records.header: RELIG 105 Jesus: A Global Biography (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: RELIG 105 Jesus: A Global Biography (5) A&H/SSc Explores how Jesus became a global icon, shaping not just Western religions but influencing cultures and traditions worldwide. Goes beyond his role in Christianity and Judaism, diving into his presence as a prophet in Islam and his impact on Asian religions. Illustrates how his teachings and legacy have transcended religious boundaries, sparking conversation, adaptation, and influence across the globe.

records.title: Yoga: Past and Present
records.header: RELIG 120 Yoga: Past and Present (5) A&H/SSc, DIV
records.text: RELIG 120 Yoga: Past and Present (5) A&H/SSc, DIV Studies yoga and its history, practice, literature, and politics. From the ancient past to modern yoga, studies essential texts and ideas, as well as the effects of class, religion, gender, nationalism, development, Marxism, colonialism, and physical culture on yoga. Offered: jointly with CHID 120; A.

records.title: Judaism: Religion and the Making of Meaning
records.header: RELIG 145 Judaism: Religion and the Making of Meaning (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 145 Judaism: Religion and the Making of Meaning (5) SSc Examines religion as a framework through which individuals and communities understand life, values, and belonging. Using Judaism as a primary example, explores Judaism's stories, rituals, laws, holidays, and beliefs as ways people make meaning and build identity. Addresses Judaism's impact on society, culture, and politics in an increasingly multicultural, religious, and interconnected world. Offered: jointly with JEW ST 145.

records.title: Heroes, Heretics, and Radicals: The Origins of Judaism and Christianity
records.header: RELIG 155 Heroes, Heretics, and Radicals: The Origins of Judaism and Christianity (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 155 Heroes, Heretics, and Radicals: The Origins of Judaism and Christianity (5) SSc Investigates the heroes, heretics, and radical pioneers of religious movements around the beginning of the Common Era (150 BCE-150 CE). Students learn to analyze primary sources, engage critically with secondary sources, and author their own historical narrative. Offered: W.

records.header: RELIG 201 Introduction to World Religions: Western Traditions (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 201 Introduction to World Religions: Western Traditions (5) SSc History of religions, concentrating on religious traditions that have developed west of the Indus. Primary attention to the Semitic religions (Judaism, Christianity, Islam) and to their ancient world background with emphasis on basic conceptual and symbolic structures.

records.header: RELIG 202 Introduction to World Religions: Eastern Traditions (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 202 Introduction to World Religions: Eastern Traditions (5) SSc History of religions, concentrating on religions that have developed in South Asia and East Asia. Primary attention to Hinduism and Buddhism; other important Asian religions are discussed in relation to them, with emphasis on basic conceptual and symbolic structures.

records.title: Religion, Violence, and Peace: Patterns Across Time and Tradition
records.header: RELIG 205 Religion, Violence, and Peace: Patterns Across Time and Tradition (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 205 Religion, Violence, and Peace: Patterns Across Time and Tradition (5) SSc Investigates the complex relationship between violence and peace in a variety of religious traditions. Examines case studies from the ancient Near East, medieval East Asia, and the contemporary West from the standpoint of lived experiences and contemporary theories derived from several academic disciplines. Offered: jointly with HUM 205/MELC 285; W.

records.title: Ancient Christianity: From Jesus to Muhammad
records.header: RELIG 209 Ancient Christianity: From Jesus to Muhammad (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 209 Ancient Christianity: From Jesus to Muhammad (5) SSc Offers a survey of ancient Christianity as it grew from a small Jewish sect into a large, predominantly gentile movement. Focuses on the broader religious landscape of the ancient Mediterranean basin and the variety of beliefs and practices attested by diverse groups of Jesus followers in the years before the rise of Islam. Offered: jointly with HSTAM 209.

records.title: Introduction to Muslim Beliefs and Practices
records.header: RELIG 211 Introduction to Muslim Beliefs and Practices (5) SSc/A&H
records.text: RELIG 211 Introduction to Muslim Beliefs and Practices (5) SSc/A&H Examines the origins and development of central beliefs in various Muslim traditions; such as monotheism, prophecy, divine judgment, and predestination. Looks at ritual and socio-cultural practices in Muslim societies in Asia, Africa, and Europe. Offered: jointly with MELC 230.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Introduction to the Quran
records.header: RELIG 212 Introduction to the Quran (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: RELIG 212 Introduction to the Quran (5) A&H/SSc A literary, historical, and theological introduction to the Quran. Looks at the historical circumstances of the text's compilation; its collection and redaction; its narrative structure; its rhetorical strategies; its major themes; its connections to and departures from the Hebrew Bible and the New Testament; commentary and exegesis; translation; and its impact on political and religious thought. Offered: jointly with MELC 231.

records.title: Introduction to the New Testament
records.header: RELIG 220 Introduction to the New Testament (5) A&H/SSc
records.text: RELIG 220 Introduction to the New Testament (5) A&H/SSc Introduction to the writings in the New Testament, their nature and origins as explored in modern scholarly research, and the first decades of the Christian religion.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Introduction to the Hebrew Bible: Old Testament
records.header: RELIG 240 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible: Old Testament (5) SSc/A&H
records.text: RELIG 240 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible: Old Testament (5) SSc/A&H Examines the Hebrew Bible (Old Testament) in translation and its relationship with literatures of ancient Near East. Comparisons drawn between Biblical text and literary works of Canaan, Egypt, Greece, Mesopotamia. Emphasis on the sophisticated literary techniques employed by Biblical writers. Offered: jointly with MELC 202.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Christianity in Asia
records.header: RELIG 242 Christianity in Asia (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 242 Christianity in Asia (5) SSc Christianity in East Asia, sixteenth century to present. Shared experiences that transcended national boundaries. Also traces divergent paths Christianity took in China, Korea, and Japan. What propelled missionary expansion? Why did people convert? What are lasting legacies of Christianity? Attention to shifting meanings of faith, identity, and religious community across the region. Offered: jointly with HSTAS 242.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: American Religions
records.header: RELIG 254 American Religions (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: RELIG 254 American Religions (5) SSc, DIV Seeks to understand religious diversity in the American context and the varieties of religions in the American historical horizon including religious minorities, American Protestants, public religious expressions, and new American religions.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Sacred Music in the European Tradition
records.header: RELIG 264 Sacred Music in the European Tradition (5) A&H
records.text: RELIG 264 Sacred Music in the European Tradition (5) A&H Surveys European and American sacred music from the twelvth to twentieth centuries, examining the important role of music in religious worship. Considers the means composers used to make musical works sound the way they do to convey the messages of the texts through music. Offered: jointly with MUSIC 264.

records.title: Religious Thought Since the Middle Ages
records.header: RELIG 305 Religious Thought Since the Middle Ages (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 305 Religious Thought Since the Middle Ages (5) SSc Development of religious thought in the West from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century. History of focal ideas: God, man, knowledge, and authority during this period and the relation of changes in these ideas to the ways in which basic issues in religious thought have been conceived.

records.title: Religion and World Politics
records.header: RELIG 307 Religion and World Politics (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: RELIG 307 Religion and World Politics (5) SSc, DIV Explores the intersection of religion and politics in various world regions, including the U.S., Europe, Middle East, Latin America, and China. Focuses on the role religious diversity plays in affecting government policy, including how state power structures privilege certain faith traditions and how political actors can be captured by religious interest groups. Includes discussion of Judaism, Christianity, Islam, and Hinduism. Offered: jointly with POL S 307.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: The Biblical Prophets
records.header: RELIG 315 The Biblical Prophets (3) A&H/SSc
records.text: RELIG 315 The Biblical Prophets (3) A&H/SSc Explores the Biblical prophets (in translation) within their Near Eastern contexts. Historicity, literary and rhetorical sophistication, and ideological agendas. Seeks to uncover the meaning and distinctiveness of Israelite prophecy within the context of the larger Near East. No knowledge of the Bible required. Offered: jointly with MELC 305.

records.title: Comparative Study of Death
records.header: RELIG 320 Comparative Study of Death (5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 320 Comparative Study of Death (5) SSc Analyzes death from a cross-cultural perspective. Topics include funerary practices, concepts of the soul and afterlife, cultural variations in grief, cemeteries as folk art, and medical and ethical issues in comparative context. Compares American death practices to those of other cultures. Offered: jointly with ANTH 322.

records.title: Comparative Religion
records.header: RELIG 321 Comparative Religion (3/5) SSc
records.text: RELIG 321 Comparative Religion (3/5) SSc Anthropological approaches to religious experience and belief with emphasis on conceptual issues such as ritual, symbolism, identity, ecstatic experience, and revitalization movements in the context of globalization. Also addresses the diversity of religious expression in American culture and how that compares with other societies. Offered: jointly with ANTH 321.

records.title: Gender, Sex, and Religion
records.header: RELIG 334 Gender, Sex, and Religion (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: RELIG 334 Gender, Sex, and Religion (5) SSc, DIV The Bible and its interpreters invented the gender categories and hierarchies that readers take for granted. Employs academic approaches that illuminate the construction of those categories and explores the debates within Judaism and Christianity as well as within academia today about gender, sex, sexuality, and religion. Offered: jointly with GWSS 334; Sp.

records.title: Islam in Africa
records.header: RELIG 338 Islam in Africa (5)
records.text: RELIG 338 Islam in Africa (5) Covers the history and diversity of Islam in Africa. Examines how Islamic belief and practice interact with local cultures, politics, and colonial legacies. Topics include legal traditions, Sufi movements, state power, and Africa's connections to the wider Islamic world and Europe. Offered: jointly with MELC 338.

records.text: RELIG 352 Hinduism (5) SSc Varieties of Hindu religious practice; the diverse patterns of religious thought and action among contemporary Hindus. Includes ritual behavior, village Hinduism, tantrism, sadhus, yoga, sects, the major gods and their mythologies, religious art, and the adjustments of Hinduism to modernity.

Includes the "Three Jewels" (i.e., the Buddha or Awakened Person, the Teaching [Dharma], and Community [Sangha]) around which Buddhism is traditionally articulated.

records.text: RELIG 380 Theories In the Study of Religion (5) SSc Provides a variety of approaches to the study of religion centered on examining the relationship between religion and modernity in the tradition of post-enlightenment, Euro-American scholarship. Examines theories of religion across disciplines: history, anthropology, sociology, Marxism, feminism, postmodernism, political theology, and Freudian psycho-analytical theory. Provides an in-depth survey of the three key genres of early and classical Muslim writing: scripture (Quran), historiography (Maghazi, Sira, and Tabaqat), and exegesis (Tafsir and Ta'wil). records.text: RELIG 440 Angels: From the Bible to American Spirituality (5) SSc Surveys conceptions of angels in foundational texts from the Bible through the Quran and explores the significance of angels in contemporary American spirituality. Though often neglected in the study of religion, angels are integral to the faith and practice of Jews, Christians, and Muslims, transcending religious boundaries in their popularity.

Attention is given to the priesthoods, personal piety, rituals of purification and healing, and the conflict of religions in the early Roman Empire. Many lectures illustrated by slides.
